title: Data Engineering Reverse-Scaffold Pedagogy

co_creators.role: Data Engineering & Intelligent Data Infrastructure Faculty Lead

educational_thesis: Students should not be promoted for reproducing explanations. They must produce traceable data-engineering artifacts, survive failure-oriented evaluation, transfer principles to unfamiliar conditions, and integrate the cohort's specialties into a defensible final thesis.

reverse_scaffold.final_state: A cohort can defend an evidence-backed enterprise data platform thesis whose sources, transformations, dependencies, security controls, failure behavior, observability, lineage, AI-data interfaces, limitations, and rollback can be reconstructed.
backward_design: Define thesis acceptance contract and invalidation conditions
Define integration competencies needed for the thesis
Define module-level evidence needed to establish each competency
Define labs that force construction, failure, diagnosis, recovery, explanation, and transfer
Matriculate only after identities, curriculum, governance, evidence rules, and thesis contract are bound

instructional_methods.rule: Every technical claim tied to a working artifact must distinguish executed evidence from proposed design.
Core pipeline/orchestration modules require at least one controlled failure case and recovery analysis when execution is available.
Students must state assumptions, rejected alternatives, dependencies, risks, and evidence gaps.
Each student must review at least one artifact outside its specialization; peer review is advisory and cannot replace independent evaluation.
Before thesis eligibility, each student must apply a learned principle to an unfamiliar data-engineering scenario without access to the original worked solution.
The final thesis must integrate contributions from all ten student specialties into one coherent governed platform argument.

cannot: replace disciplinary evidence with governance compliance

a_code_mapping.A01_intake: Register cohort, students, faculty, and thesis intent
a_code_mapping.A02_alignment: Bind mission, learning goals, constraints, and evidence rules
a_code_mapping.A03_scoping: Define module outcomes, thesis boundaries, and success criteria
a_code_mapping.A04_data_gather: Collect source material, datasets, specifications, and prior evidence
a_code_mapping.A05_screen: Check prerequisites, provenance, integrity, and obvious gaps
a_code_mapping.A06_evaluate: Evaluate artifacts and alternative designs using independent evidence
a_code_mapping.A07_risk: Assess correctness, security, privacy, operational, lineage, and failure risks
a_code_mapping.A08_options: Compare architectural alternatives and remediation paths
a_code_mapping.A09_decision_gate: Matriculation, module progression exceptions, and thesis gate decisions
a_code_mapping.A10_execute: Build/run approved labs, pipelines, and thesis components
a_code_mapping.A11_monitor: Track quality, execution evidence, drift, failures, and learning progress
a_code_mapping.A12_review: Retrospective; update pedagogy only from documented cohort evidence

pedagogy_effectiveness_measures: module artifact pass rate by first attempt and after remediation
confidence calibration where probabilistic judgments are used
effectiveness_boundary: Pedagogy approval establishes governance/design fitness only. It does not establish educational effectiveness until observed cohort evidence exists.
rollback: If evidence shows a teaching method harms transfer, traceability, correctness, or thesis quality, revert that method to the prior version while preserving the cohort evidence and A12 review.
